text.p: German construction group Bilfinger + Berger Bau AG said on Tuesday that it expected to report satisfactory earnings for full-year 1997.

"Presuming we can compensate for falling earnings at home by positive growth in our foreign business, for 1997 we expect to see construction output at around the same levels seen last year and, once again, satisfactory earnings," the group said in its annual report.
Bilfinger's construction output rose 11.4 percent to 2.83 billion marks in the first four months of 1997.

But the company predicted a 1.2 percent drop in construction output to 9.133 billion marks in the full 1997 year due to its selective approach to accepting new orders and because of weakness in the domestic building industry.
"In the current business year our domestic construction output will fall," management board chairman Christian Roth said in the text of a speech released ahead of Bilfinger's annual news conference.
"This is not just a result of the economic and structural problems in the German construction industry, but also because of our particularly selective stance in tendering for contracts."
